_readme: Hand-maintained inputs for the Brazil Production page (src/brazilprod.py).
Everything else on that page is pulled live and free (USDA PS&D, EIA).
countries_curated - country-level output for commodities with no free API
(metals via USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, pulp, ethanol).
Refresh once a year, Jan/Feb, when the new MCS lands.
'world' is the published world total and is authoritative: the
listed countries are only the majors and the page buckets the
rest into 'Other'. If the listed countries ever sum to MORE than
'world', the build flags it rather than silently redefining world.
companies         - who produces Brazil's share. Refresh quarterly from company
'basis' says WHAT the company number measures - production, equity share, crush,
slaughter or export. Never mix bases in one block: a soybean exporter did not grow
the beans. 'confidence': reported = straight off a company release; association =
industry body; estimate = desk estimate, shown with a caveat on the page and PDF.

ANM AMB (Anuario Mineral Brasileiro) does NOT carry the title-holder - it is aggregated to Ano base x UF x Classe Substancia x Substancia. Verified 2026-08-24 against the live files. The company-level route is CFEM (royalty returns), wired in src/anmdata.py; it reports volume SOLD, and only iron ore and bauxite reconcile against their national figures because the rest are published as contained metal.

pulp.label: Wood pulp
pulp.note: Brazil is a mid-table producer of ALL wood pulp but the clear world number one in traded hardwood (eucalyptus) market pulp, where it is roughly a third of global supply.

iron_ore.source: Company production reports (Vale 4Q24, CSN Mineracao, Anglo American, Usiminas)
iron_ore.note: Attributable saleable production. Samarco is a 50/50 Vale-BHP JV and is shown separately, not inside Vale.
iron_ore.unsourced_reason: Live from ANM's CFEM royalty returns (src/anmdata.py) when the store exists. This block is only the fallback shown if data/signals/anm_metals.json is missing - run the daily pull, or `python src/anmdata.py`.

crude_oil.source: ANP monthly production bulletin + company disclosures
crude_oil.note: Working-interest (equity) share of Brazilian liquids, NOT operatorship. Petrobras operates far more than it owns - it is the operator of most pre-salt fields in which Shell, TotalEnergies, CNOOC, CNPC, Equinor, Galp and Repsol Sinopec hold equity.

pulp.source: Company results releases + Iba (Industria Brasileira de Arvores)
pulp.note: Chemical wood pulp production in Brazil. Veracel is a Suzano / Stora Enso JV, shown separately.

rows.company: Other (Arauco, Sylvamo, integrated and non-market mills)

pulp.unsourced_reason: Suzano publishes, but not on this table's basis. Its 20-F reports MARKET PULP SALES (10,864,630 t in 2024) and nominal capacity (13.44 Mt), while the national figure is chemical wood pulp PRODUCED - which includes pulp a mill integrates into its own paper and never sells. Klabin, CMPC, Bracell, Eldorado, Cenibra and Veracel are B3-listed or private and publish only in IR PDFs. Verified 2026-08-25.

sugar.source: Company reports read directly; national crush from UNICA (2026-08-25)
sugar.note: Cane CRUSHED in the 2025/26 harvest, against Brazil's 667.58 Mt from UNICA's own sector snapshot. Only groups that publish their own crush appear. UNICAdata has no company dimension - checked directly - so the ~340 remaining mills cannot be attributed and sit in one unsourced line. Crush share is applied to Brazil's SUGAR output to size the hedge, which assumes a group's sugar/ethanol mix matches the national mix; it does not exactly.

rows.document: Raizen Relatorio Integrado 2025/26 - business model page

rows.detail: calendar 2025; the crush season runs Apr-Dec so it maps to this harvest
Atvos, BP Bioenergy, Tereos, CMAA, Coruripe and ~340 other mills. No industry body publishes crush by group, so these are unknown.

beef.note: Share of federally-inspected cattle slaughter, not of herd ownership. Cattle are RAISED on tens of thousands of private ranches; these are the processors that buy and slaughter them.
beef.unsourced_reason: The processors publish capacity and tonnes SOLD, not carcass-weight slaughter. JBS's 20-F gives facility counts and daily head capacity; the national figure is 12.37 Mt CWE from IBGE. Those do not reconcile without assuming a yield and a utilisation rate, which would be inventing two numbers to produce a third. Verified 2026-08-25.

chicken.note: Share of Brazilian broiler output. Integrators own the birds and contract the growing out, so this is closer to a true production share than the beef table.
chicken.unsourced_reason: Same basis problem as beef: BRF and JBS Seara report volumes sold in tonnes of product, while the national figure is bird output. Marfrig and BRF merged into MBRF during 2025, so the 2024 entities no longer file separately either. Verified 2026-08-25.

soybeans.source: SLC Agricola operational data, read directly (2026-08-25)
soybeans.note: Brazil has no material corporate soybeans producer. SLC Agricola is the largest listed grower and is under 1% of the crop; the rest is tens of thousands of independent farms, which is a fact about the market rather than a gap in the data. SLC publishes planted AREA and YIELD, not tonnage, so production here is area x yield from the same table - arithmetic on two published figures, not an estimate. SLC's realised 2024/25 harvest is set against the national 2025/26 figure; at under 1% of the crop the year offset does not move the share. INTERNAL ONLY - this is a prospect list, not a producer ranking, and it is kept out of the client PDF.

rows.document: SLC Agricola 'Dados Operacionais' 2T26 workbook, tables 1 and 2 (safra 2024/25 realizado)

rows.detail: Tens of thousands of private farms and co-operatives.

corn.source: SLC Agricola operational data, read directly (2026-08-25)
corn.note: Brazil has no material corporate corn producer. SLC Agricola is the largest listed grower and is under 1% of the crop; the rest is tens of thousands of independent farms, which is a fact about the market rather than a gap in the data. SLC publishes planted AREA and YIELD, not tonnage, so production here is area x yield from the same table - arithmetic on two published figures, not an estimate. SLC's realised 2024/25 harvest is set against the national 2025/26 figure; at under 1% of the crop the year offset does not move the share. INTERNAL ONLY - this is a prospect list, not a producer ranking, and it is kept out of the client PDF.

rows.document: SLC Agricola 'Dados Operacionais' 2T26 workbook, tables 1 and 2 (safra 2024/25 realizado)

rows.detail: Tens of thousands of private farms and co-operatives.

coffee.note: Brazil's crop comes from roughly 300,000 growers. Cooxupe is a growers' co-operative, so it is the one line here that is genuinely upstream.
coffee.unsourced_reason: Cecafe's monthly report - read directly, November 2024, 23 pages - breaks exports down by destination, port, state and arabica/robusta, but carries NO exporter ranking. Company-level customs data is confidential in Brazil, so this needs paid bill-of-lading data. Verified 2026-08-25.

cotton.note: Cotton is the one Brazilian row crop with real farm-level concentration - large Mato Grosso and Bahia estates. SLC Agricola discloses its own lint volumes; the rest are private groups.
cotton.unsourced_reason: ABRAPA state data plus SLC Agricola disclosures. Not yet wired.

niobium.source: Company disclosures + USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries
niobium.note: Brazil is ~90% of world niobium and Brazilian niobium is essentially one private company: CBMM's Araxa operation in Minas Gerais. There is no listed pure-play - CBMM is held by the Moreira Salles group with Japanese, Korean and Chinese minority stakes.
niobium.unsourced_reason: CBMM is private and publishes no tonnage. CFEM carries CMOC Brasil's concentrate tonnage, but the national figure is CONTAINED NIOBIUM and the conversion needs a grade we do not have, so no split is published.

bauxite.source: Company production reports (Hydro, Alcoa) + MRN disclosures
bauxite.note: Mineracao Rio do Norte is a joint venture whose shareholders include Vale, South32, Rio Tinto and CBA, so its output is not attributable to any single listed parent.
bauxite.unsourced_reason: Live from ANM's CFEM royalty returns (src/anmdata.py) when the store exists. This block is only the fallback shown if data/signals/anm_metals.json is missing - run the daily pull, or `python src/anmdata.py`.

copper.source: Company annual filings and results releases, read directly (2026-08-25)
copper.note: CONTAINED copper, the same basis as the national figure. Brazilian operations only: Vale's Canadian and Indonesian output is excluded, as is Ero's gold. ANM's CFEM returns cannot supply this - they declare ore and concentrate tonnage, and converting that to contained metal needs a per-mine grade.

rows.document: Vale 20-F 2025, copper finished production by ore source
Lundin Mining Q4 and Full Year 2024 Results
Ero Copper 40-F 2025, Q4 MD&A operating results

rows.detail: The rest of Brazil's 400 kt. We have not sourced who produces it.

nickel.source: Company annual filings and results releases, read directly (2026-08-25)
nickel.note: CONTAINED nickel, the same basis as the national figure. Anglo American's entire nickel business was Brazilian (Barro Alto and Codemin) and was sold to MMG during 2025, so the 2024 figure is Anglo's. Atlantic Nickel's Santa Rita is privately held and publishes no volume, which is most of the gap below.

rows.document: Anglo American Q4 2024 Production Report, p16
Vale 20-F 2025, nickel finished production by ore source

rows.detail: The rest of Brazil's 88 kt, chiefly Atlantic Nickel (Santa Rita), which is private.

gold.source: Company production reports + ANM / IBGM estimates of artisanal output
gold.note: Garimpo - artisanal and small-scale mining, concentrated in Para, Amazonas and Roraima - is the single largest source of Brazilian gold, ahead of any listed miner. It is shown as its own line because it is a real producer but not a company. Treat this split with more caution than the other tables: a meaningful share of garimpo output is unlicensed and enters the legal chain through trading desks, so the national total it is measured against is itself uncertain.
gold.unsourced_reason: CFEM carries per-filer gold, but its unit field cannot be trusted for this substance: filers declare ore tonnage under a gram unit, so the declared quantities sum to roughly a thousand times world production. Separating metal from ore would need an assumed gold price and royalty rate - modelling, not sourcing. Artisanal (garimpo) output is in any case not reliably measured by anyone.

_provenance_key.live: fetched this run from a machine-readable source (USDA PS&D, EIA, ANP)
_provenance_key.keyed: typed in from a named published document a human can re-check
_provenance_key.names_only: we know who the producers are, NOT how much each makes - volumes blank
